title: DMT Microdoses: Positive Mood Impact | Microdosinginstitute
abstract:
- Chronic, intermittent microdoses of DMT produced significant improvements in mood and reductions in depressive behavior in rats, highlighting its potential therapeutic effects without the typical anxiety caused by higher doses.
- The study found no adverse effects on memory or social behaviors due to the microdosing regimen, although it did not replicate the cognitive benefits reported in human studies.
- DMT treatment resulted in increased body weight among male rats, suggesting potential metabolic effects of microdosing not fully understood in the scope of this research.
## Discussion  
The findings suggested that chronic, intermittent low doses of DMT could play a role in enhancing mood and alleviating anxiety through mechanisms different from those of acute, hallucinogenic doses. The DMT treatment appeared to elevate the excitability of specific neurons linked to fear and behavior, indicating underlying biochemical alterations that necessitate further investigation. The differential effects between genders, particularly the decrease in dendritic spine density observed only in females, also emphasized the necessity for understanding the implications of what could be a gender-specific response to DMT microdosing.  
Ultimately, while the study presented a compelling case for the benefits of psychedelic microdosing in treating mood and anxiety disorders, it also highlighted the importance of researching potential risks. Careful examination of neurodevelopmental impacts and age-related responses to microdosing remains essential in furthering knowledge on this topic. Given the potential benefits observed, psychedelic microdosing may serve as a promising avenue in preventing or minimizing symptoms associated with depression and anxiety.
### Chronic, Intermittent Microdoses of the Psychedelic N, N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) Produce Positive Effects on Mood and Anxiety in Rodents
